_meta.description: Private well water data for Montrose, Delta, Ouray counties. The largest and least contested content opportunity — no competitor covers this.
_meta.keyInsight: Depth is the story: drilling deeper solves selenium and uranium but NOT iron and manganese.

regulatoryVacuum.quote: CDPHE does not regulate water quality for private water wells because they are not covered by the Safe Drinking Water Act.
regulatoryVacuum.sdwaThreshold: Applies only to systems serving 25+ people 60+ days/year, or with 15+ service connections
regulatoryVacuum.cdpheRecommendation: Test at least annually; more often if pregnant or breastfeeding people drink the water, unexplained stomach illness, contaminants found in a neighboring well, or any change in taste/odor/color/clarity
regulatoryVacuum.dataGap: CDPHE's private-well repository is incomplete because testing is voluntary and private labs generally do not report results to the Tracking Program.

sixCountyStudy.headline: 56% of tested wells exceeded one or more primary or secondary standards (58% including lead and copper). 15% exceeded a primary standard.

nationalComparison.sulfate: 18.34% vs 3.79% nationally — roughly 5x, attributed to pyrite

shallowVsDeep._note: USGS Water Quality Portal + USGS SIR 2019-5029. The single strongest technical argument on the site.

shallow.definition: <50 ft, alluvium overlying Mancos Shale, east side of the Uncompahgre

shallowVsDeep.takeaway: Depth solves selenium and uranium. It does NOT solve iron and manganese — those stay elevated at every depth. That distinction drives the correct treatment recommendation and no competitor makes it.

mancosShaleMechanism.selenium: Naturally present in Mancos Shale, leached by irrigation. Primary source area is the east side of the Uncompahgre River in Delta and Montrose counties.
mancosShaleMechanism.nitrate: Range <0.04 to 550 mg/L as N, median 4.8 mg/L as N (n=70). USGS: 'the primary source is the Mancos Shale' — NOT fertilizer.
mancosShaleMechanism.coupling: Nitrate as low as 5 mg/L as N maintains oxidizing conditions that inhibit selenate reduction, keeping selenium mobile.
mancosShaleMechanism.groundwaterAge: 6 to 20 years — recharged by irrigation, no deeper recharge source found
mancosShaleMechanism.honestyNote: USGS states 'few wells are used for drinking-water supply' in the Uncompahgre Project irrigated area. Do NOT imply these shallow monitoring wells are typical domestic supply wells. Frame as: this is what the shallow aquifer under irrigated ground looks like, which is why depth and testing matter.

uravanBelt.location: Western Montrose County — Nucla, Naturita, Uravan, Gateway, Bull Canyon
uravanBelt.geology: 70 x 30 mile belt. Uranium, vanadium, radium ore in the Jurassic Salt Wash Member of the Morrison Formation. ~1,200 small mines.
uravanBelt.study: CGS/CDPHE 5-year Baseline Radiological Study, Year 3 report CGS Open-File Report OF-24-08 (Sebol and Buch-Leviatan, 2024)
uravanBelt.uraniumDetail: Detected at 19 of 23 locations; 1 exceeded 0.030 mg/L (a 150-ft well in mudstone).
uravanBelt.arsenicDetail: Above reporting limit at 6 locations; 5 exceeded 0.01 mg/L.

radon.indoorAir: About half of Colorado homes exceed the EPA action level of 4.0 pCi/L. CDPHE distributed 12,500+ free test kits in early 2025 and mitigated 200+ homes.
radon.epaZones: Zone 1 = predicted average indoor screening >4 pCi/L; Zone 2 = 2-4; Zone 3 = <2. EPA states all homes should be tested regardless of zone.

mancosNote: Mancos Shale is a regional confining unit, but locally wells are completed in weathered Mancos Shale at shallow depths.

permitting.database: Colorado DWR Well Permit Search Tool and Well Permit Map Viewer — searchable by permit number, name, address, or subdivision
permitting.householdUseOnlyUnder35Acres: Inside one single-family dwelling only; no outdoor use
permitting.over35Acres: Up to three single-family dwellings, watering of domestic animals, and irrigation of no more than one acre of lawn and garden
permitting.agriculturalNitrateStandard: Colorado's agricultural groundwater standard for nitrate is 100 mg/L as N — the drinking-water MCL is 10 mg/L as N. Do not confuse them.

countyHealthDepartments.montrose: Environmental Health states private well quality is not regulated and is the owner's responsibility; maintains a list of Western Slope certified labs.
countyHealthDepartments.delta: Does not test or regulate private well quality, but a water sample report is required for new wells and subdivision applications. Sample containers via Mesa County Public Health; analysis at Grand Junction Regional Laboratory or the CDPHE state lab.

freeTestingProgram.contentAngle: A genuinely useful thing to tell homeowners. Builds trust and costs Ken nothing.

epaSecondaryMCLs.note: EPA does not enforce secondary standards.
